name: Isle of Skye (Ian Macleod blend)
house_style: A blended Scotch — NOT a single malt. Peated island malt (a Skye core, widely understood to lean on Talisker) softened by Speyside and Highland malts plus grain whisky; the house signature is gentle maritime smoke wrapped in honeyed orchard fruit, baking spice and oak rather than aggressive peat.
notes: Blend created in 1933 by a Skye-born blender named Ian Macleod from a 'secret family recipe', conceived as an homage to Clan Macleod (seat: Dunvegan Castle, Isle of Skye). The brand is owned by Ian Macleod Distillers (the company acquired it in 1963). Unusually deep core range spanning 8, 12, 18, 21, 25 and 30 Year Old. All expressions bottled at 40% ABV. The 25YO was named Best Blended Scotch Whisky in the World at the 2025 San Francisco World Spirits Competition; the 30YO took Gold at the 2026 World Whiskies Awards. IMPORTANT: 'Isle of Skye' the blend is distinct from the Talisker single malt distillery on Skye.

ian_macleod.company_facts: Owned by Ian Macleod Distillers — independent, family-owned (Russell family), HQ Broxburn, founded 1933 by Leonard Russell Snr; the company is a principal blended brand alongside Smokehead and King Robert. (Brand created 1933; acquired by the company 1963.) Produces >15M bottles/yr group-wide.
